G3766.definition: adv. (οὔκουν, not therefore), ; with the negative element lost, therefore, so then: Jhn.18:37.†; (AS)

G3700.definition: ὀπτάνω; late present as from ὤφθην (= ὁράω); mid., ὀπτάνομαι, to allow oneself to be seen, to appear. with dative, Act.1:3. (For exx. from π., see Deiss., LAE, 79, 2526; MM, ii, xviii.) †; (AS)

G3706.definition: (ὁράω)  ; 1. in Arist. and later writers, the act of seeing, the sense of sight, and by meton., pl., the eyes. ; 2. appearance (Num.24:4, Eze.1:5, Sir.41:20, al.): Rev.4:3. ; 3. = ὅραμα, a vision: Act.2:17 (LXX), Rev.9:17.†; (AS)

G3741.definition: (so sometimes in cl., but most frequently -α, -ον),  ; religiously right, right­eous, pious, Holy: of men, Tit.1:8. Heb.7:26; by meton., ὁ. χεῖρας, 1Ti.2:8 (cf. Deu.32:4); of God, Rev.15:4 16:5; as subst., ὁ ὅ., of the Messiah, Act.2:27 13:35" (LXX) ; τὰ ὅ. Δανεὶδ τ. πιστά (Field, Notes, 121), Act.13:34 (LXX).†; SYN.: see: ἅγιος (cf. also DB, ii, 399.b; iv, 352.b, and ref. see word -ίως) (AS)

G3791.definition: (ὄχλος),  ; to move, disturb; hence, generally, to trouble, vex: pass., Act.5:6 (act. absol., = pass., to be in a tumult, 3Mac, l.with; cf. ἐν-, παρ-εν-οχλέω, and see MM, xviii).†; (AS)

G3730.definition: 1. a violent movement, impulse: Jas.3:4; 2. a hostile movement, onset, assault. Act.14:5.†; (AS)

G3717.definition: straight; (a) in height, straight, upright: Act.14:10; (b) in line, straight, direct: figuratively, Heb.12:13 (LXX).†; (AS)

G3792.definition: ὀχλο-ποιέω, -ῶ ; to gather a crowd, make a riot: Act.17:5 (not elsewhere).†; (AS)

G3734.definition: (ὅρος, a boundary, + τίθημι) ; a setting of boundaries; in pl., bounds; Act.17:26.†; (AS)

G3712.definition: (ὀρέγω), ; the length of the outstretched arms, a fathom: Act.27:28.†; (AS)

G3715.definition: (ὀρέγομαι),  ; the most general ward for all kinds of desire, longing, appetite: of lust, Rom.1:27 ; SYN.: see: πάθος (AS)

G3785.definition: ὄφελον 2 aorist of ὀφείλω, without the augment (see M, Pr., 201n), used to express a fruitless wish; in cl. with an infin. (chiefly poët.), ; would that: with indic. aor., 1Co.4:8; impf., 2Co.11:1, Rev.3:15; fut., Gal.5:12 (a practicable wish, see 131., 206 f., 220. The construction with indic. is only found in late writers.)†; (AS)

G3740.definition: (ὅσος), ; relat. adv., ; as often as: before ἐάν (which see), 1Co.11:25-26, Rev.11:6,†; (AS)

G3750.definition: (ὀσφραίνομαι, to smell), ; the sense of smell, smell­ing: 1Co.12:17.†; (AS)

G3749.definition: (ὄστρακον, an earthen vessel or potsherd),  ; made of clay, earthen: 2Co.4:7, 2Ti.2:20.†; (AS)

G3794.definition: (ὀχυρόω, to fortify, make firm),  ; a stronghold, fortress (Psa.89:40, Nam.3:12, 14 al.); in LXX and NT, also metaphorically of that in which confidence is placed (Pro.10:29 21:22, al.): 2Co.10:4.†; (AS)

G3716.definition: (ὀρθό-πους, going straight), ; = cl. εὐθυπορέω, to walk straight: metaphorically, Gal.2:14 (not elsewhere).†; (AS)

G3787.definition: ὀφθαλμο-δουλία (Rec. -εία), -ας, ἡ ; (ὀφθαλμός, δοῦλος), ; eye-service: Eph.6:6, Col.3:22 (not found elsewhere).†; (AS)

G3743.definition: (ὅσιος), ; adv.,  ; piously, holily: ὁ. καὶ δικαίως κ. ἀμέμπτως (on the distinction here between these synonyms, see M, Th., 24 f.), 1Th.2:10.†; (AS)

G3713.definition: to reach, stretch out; pass. and mid., to stretch oneself out, reach forth; metaphorically, to reach after, grasp at, aspire to: with genitive of thing(s), 1Ti.3:1, Heb.11:16; φιλαργυρίας (see Ellic. and CGT, in l), 1Ti.6:10.†; SYN.: ἐπιθυμέω, to desire (which see) (AS)

G3718.definition: (- ὀρθός, τέμνω),  ; to cut straight, as a road (τ. ὁδούς, figuratively, Pr, ll with). Metaphorical, τ. λόγον τ. ἀληθείας, 2Ti.2:15 (V. Ellic. and CGT, in l; not found elsewhere).†; (AS)

G3728.definition: (ὅρκος, ὄμνυμι; by metapl. for τὰ ὁρκωμόσια, asseverations on oath; see MM, xviii),  ; affirmation on oath, an oath: Heb.7:20-21, 28.†; (AS)

G3797.definition: (ὀψέ),  ; poët. and late for ὄψιος, late: ὑετὸς ὄ., ; the latter rain (see DB, see word "rain"), with ellipsis of ὑετός (see WM, 740), Ja 57.†; (AS)

G3703.definition: 1. late summer, early autumn (the time between the risings of Sirius and Arcturus, i.e. late July, all August and early September). ; 2. By meton. (as being fruit-time), ripe fruits Rev.18:14 (cf. φθινοπωρινά, Ju 12).†; (AS)
